articleTitle: Second Harmonic Laser Voltage Imaging on FinFET Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: Second harmonic Laser Voltage Imaging (LVI) is a laser-based fault isolation technique that maps the duty cycle degradation of the targeted circuitry. This paper presents successful case studies that captures anomalies in scan chain using second harmonic LVI on sub-10nm FinFET devices.

articleTitle: Accurate Unknown Identification of Dark Colored Contamination with Sub-Micron Infrared (O-PTIR) and Reflection Mode FT-IR Spectroscopies
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: Accurate molecular analysis of rough, dark-colored contamination particles extracted from the cross-sectioned underfill region is usually a challenging task with conventional spectroscopic tools. Combining conventional reflection mode Fourier-transform infrared (r-FTIR) and sub-micron infrared spectroscopies (Optical PhotoThermal InfraRed or O-PTIR), the chemistry near the surface and of the bulk can be effectively evaluated. The combined analysis yields a highly specific set of chemical information for pinpointing the potential origin of contamination particles in the microelectronic package.

articleTitle: Design Optimization of Stacked-NMOS ESD Protection for Mixed-Voltage Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: In this study, we optimized the stacked-NMOS design in 0.13 μm BCD technology to improve ESD performance and overvoltage tolerance. This was achieved by modifying the N<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup> drain junction to reduce the electric field at the poly/drain overlap region and ensure a more uniformly and deep total current distribution.

articleTitle: Improved Defect Detection of Advanced Semiconductor Packaging in Acoustic Imaging
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: Subtle defect in advanced packages has become invisible in conventional acoustic time-domain imaging. Acoustic Z-Gate collects image and A-scan waveform information in one file, enabling signal post-processing. This paper presents a case study using fast Mexican hat wavelet filtering of Z-Gate file to detect subtle defect. The same filtering technique is also demonstrated to isolate defect depth in a stacked X3D package. Early results using signal-based machine learning, from a small training Z-Gate dataset, to automate defect detection in X3D package are also presented.

articleTitle: The Influence of Gate-Series-Resistor on the ESD Protection and Switching Speed for 650V GaNHEMT Circuit
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: Unlike CMOS technology, there only exist two components, HEMT and resistor, that can be used to design as the electrostatic-discharge (ESD) protection circuit in GaN technology. Although HEMT has very robust ESD capability, it still cannot work very well without the resistor to clamp the ESD current or pull up the gate voltage to turn on its channel. So, most ESD protection circuits for protected HEMT are composed of resistor and HEMT. In general, the protection capability of an ESD protection circuit is determined by the size of ESD HEMT and the resistor resistance. However, the high-resistance resistor degrades the switching speed of protected HEMT, while the low-resistance resistor degrades the protection capability of ESD protection circuit. In this paper, how the turn-on gate resistor (Rg<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ON</inf>) affects the protection capability of all-terminal ESD protection circuit for a 650V GaN HEM is studied. From the test results, this protection circuit is demonstrated that can protect the gate of protected HEMT against 1 kV HBM strike for any zapping condition even if the Rg<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ON</inf> is only 2ohm.

articleTitle: Use of Low Dose Sample Preparation Method for Low-K Material
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: In this paper we investigated the low-K material shrinkage effects under electron beam exposure in FIB for TEM sample preparation. Different electron dose levels in combination with electron beam voltage have been evaluated. Optimal combination of electron beam current/voltage setting for low dose sample preparation is implemented for minimizing low-k material deformation to ensure accurate trench measurements in the subsequent TEM analysis

articleTitle: Identification Of Recovering Idss Failure Mode Via Novel Comprehensive Failure Analysis Technique For Mosfet Device
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: Failure analysis (FA) plays an important role in the semiconductor industry as the process technology and new packaging continuously improve. Device recovery is a growing challenge in the FA field. In this paper, a novel FA method is introduced using combination of electrical characteristics, a precise fault isolation and a Focused Ion Beam (FIB) together with mechanical cross section. By employing this technique, it helps to resolve the issue of failure recovery and efficiently identify the precise root cause of the failure mechanism. In the deficiency of proper FA steps perform on the recoverable drain to source leakage failure might have the tendency to miss the evidence and provide an impropriate FA result or conclusion. The conclusion can be misleading if the exact root cause is not properly addressed and corrected. The chance of failure reoccurrence is very high. Two separate investigations with varying failure mechanisms will discuss the above-mentioned techniques. Significant results of wafer related issue and foreign material issue were able to identify by applying this novel FA technique. In summary, this work introduces a novel comprehensive failure analysis that enables the identification of a device's failure mechanism. Hence, the device recovery issue is resolved, and the production team is equipped with a precise failure mechanism to investigate the cause of the failure.

articleTitle: TransNet: Automatic Classification Network for Nanoscale Wafer SEM Defects
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: Defect analysis is crucial for semiconductor manufacturing processes, especially for nanoscale processes. Automated classification of SEM defects can assist engineers in identifying root causes more quickly, thereby improving yield. We presents a comprehensive approach using a combination of Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and Transformer networks for classifying wafer defects in semiconductor manufacturing processes. By fusing CNN and Transformer networks, we achieve accurate defect classification with fewer parameters. Experimental results using a real 12-inch wafer fab dataset demonstrate a classification accuracy of 97.25<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>, even when dealing with an unbalanced dataset. Consequently, our method significantly improves the performance of SEM defect image classification.

articleTitle: Impact Analysis of Negative Gate Voltage on SiCMOS Reliability Under OFF-State Avalanche Stress
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: This paper fully researches and analyzes the effect of negative OFF-state gate-source bias voltage (V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">GS</inf>, off) on the device degradation under OFF-state avalanche stress. It is found that the degradation associated with negative V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">GS</inf>,off is much greater than that of 0V V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">GS</inf>,off and negative bias temperature instability (NBTI). While the shift in threshold voltage (V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">T</inf>) and on-resistance (R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">on</inf>) are relatively small, and the biggest change is reverse leakage current (I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Dss</inf>) corresponds to the generation of interface state. This phenomenon is analyzed in conjunction with Technology Computer Aided Design (TCAD) analysis, which demonstrate that under the avalanche stress condition, the electric field at the bottom of the gate oxide attains substantial magnitudes. Moreover, the introduction of negative V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">GS</inf>,off significantly amplifies the electric field in this region, which has a significant impact on the long-term reliability of the device.

articleTitle: Improving Reliability of IWO Thin Film Transistors with ZrAlOx via Varying AlOx/ZrOx Deposition Sequence in ALD
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: In this study, we report on the electrical characteristics and material analyses of indium tungsten oxide thin film transistors (IWO-TFTs) with zirconium aluminum oxide (ZrAlO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>) through various AlO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>/ZrO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf> deposition sequences using atomic layer deposition (ALD). The fabricated device had a positive threshold voltage (V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">T</inf>) of 0.6 V, an impressive I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">on</inf>/I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">off</inf> value of approximately 7.2×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</sup>, a subthreshold swing (SS) of 93 mV/dec, an interface trap density (N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">it</inf>) of 4.7×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</sup> cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−2</sup>, and a remarkably high degree of stability against positive bias stress (PBS). In conclusion, aluminum oxide into zirconium oxide which resulted in a smaller dielectric surface roughness (0.19 nm), thereby obtaining the enhanced mobility of IWO-TFTs. Consequently, zirconium oxide (ZrO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>) rather than aluminum oxide (AlO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>) as the contacted material for IWO film makes the device outperform by adjusting the ZrO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>/AlO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf> deposition order. These results contribute to optimizing IWO TFTs with ZrAlO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf> dielectric by showcasing improved stability by adjusting the interface between the channel and dielectric layer.

articleTitle: A printable metallic ink containing biphasic alloys for highly-reliable stretchable circuits
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: Liquid metals are ideal materials for fabricating stretchable circuits in wearable devices, becoming printable metallic inks with high conductivity by blending with solid nanoparticles. However, challenges related to reliability arise, including variation of printing patterns, and electrical damage during repeated stretching. Here, we report a novel metallic ink containing biphasic alloys, obtained by annealing the liquid metal-based mixture. The solid-phasic alloy adheres to the surface of nanoparticles, creating an anchoring effect with liquid-phasic alloy to enhance the reliability of stretchable circuits based on this novel printable metallic ink.

articleTitle: 3D System-in-Package Failure Analysis by High-Resolution Time-Domain Reflectometry
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: The rise of 3D high-bandwidth-memory (HBM) technology has boosted System-in-Package (SiP) storage density and energy efficiency. However, this advancement poses significant challenges in pinpointing defects within HBMs during package-level failure analysis. Although electro-optic sampling-based time-domain reflectometry (EOS-TDR) offers high resolution for defect isolation in packages, its effectiveness diminishes within HBMs due to reduced signal amplitude and manufacturing tolerances. To enhance EOS-TDR's efficiency in analyzing HBM failures, this study explores two waveform analysis techniques: normalization and near-die correction. Normalization extracts abnormal reflections caused by defects within the die, while near-die correction refines normalization results by minimizing sample-to-sample variations within the chip package. Results demonstrate that employing both normalization and near-die correction techniques effectively identifies open defects within HBMs.

articleTitle: Application of ICP-MS to identify the source of Metallic Contamination
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: Inductively Coupled Plasma Mass Spectrometry (ICP-MS) is being widely used in semiconductor industry to analyze the metallic contents of chemicals used in the wafer fabrication process. In this paper, application of ICP-MS to identify the types and source of metallic contaminations in solvents used in the lithography step, which subsequently translated to become particles affecting the lithography process and causing the wafers to fail was discussed. Two case studies were presented in this paper.

articleTitle: Failure Analysis on Superluminescent Diode
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: A super luminescent diode (SLED or SLD) is an edge-emitting semiconductor light source that relies on super luminescence. SLDs are ideal for use in Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT) Imaging Systems. In this paper, we reported the failure analysis plan and method for rejections from the SLD lifetime test. The failure modes for the SLD reliability test have been defined. A failure analysis flowchart was designed to identify the failure location, from the package to the chip. A scanning optical microscope (SOM), a liquid nitrogen-cooled InGasAs emission microscope, and a liquid nitrogen-cooled thermal emission microscope were used for fault isolation. An optical microscope (OM) and a scanning electron microscope (SEM) were employed to inspect the hotspot locations. Subsequently, a physical analysis was conducted on the failing location, and the failure mechanism was studied. Planar and cross-section TEM laminae were prepared using a dual-beam FIB. TEM EDX analysis was conducted on the cross-section TEM sample. The EDX analysis reveals that there is no obvious difference in element distribution, suggesting that no thermal diffusion occurred and the failure was solely due to material degradation.

articleTitle: Automotive Electronics EOS Failure Analysis and Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: Automobile industry has dramatically changed over past two decades. All OEMs start to integrate more IC components and implement high-end technology functions. Among automotive electronics failure, EOS related issue always takes the highest failure rate. This paper identifies failure analysis of component ESD failure, board level and system level EOS failure. Related diagnosis process and root cause identification are also shared.

articleTitle: Fault localization on Test Coverage and Functional Issue for SoC Product with Combining Bench and Pattern Test
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: With the rapid development of System on Chip (SoC) products, the structures and functions have become increasingly complex. Failure analysis is crucial for discovering design bugs and enhancing the quality of SoC products[1]. To improve yield and screen out the defects, Automatic Test Equipment (ATE) was particularly key tool to complete test. Automatic Test Pattern Generation(ATPG) and functional pattern on ATE were the most important test method for SoC products to confirm whether the circuit has manufacturing defects or not. In the meanwhile, the FA team often receives failed products returned from customers with test coverage issues, so that functional failure could only be duplicated on evaluation board (EVB) platform in bench level. The failure configuration is usually more flexible for debugging and modification on EVB compared to the ATE tester. Based on internal signal testability of ATPG pattern and configuration flexibility of EVB test, in this paper novel failure analysis (FA) workflow was proposed that combined bench and pattern testing to complete failure investigation and fault localization for test coverage and functional issues. And three real cases were presented to demonstrate the effectiveness of this workflow, that was beneficial in overcoming challenges, improving the success rate and reducing analysis time for complicated cases in FA.

articleTitle: Techniques and Applications of Plasma Focused Ion Beam in Silicon Die Delayering
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: Plasma Focused Ion Beam (PFIB) has emerged as a reliable silicon die delayering tool particularly for advanced nodes devices. Xenon PFIB is shown to have high controllability and precision in exposing BEOL layer, suitable for SEM inspection using the least damaging electron beam. Ion beam irradiation is known to physically damage sample surface, 30 kV Xenon beam penetrates deep into copper metallization which negatively impact nanoprobing electrical characterization. PFIB delayering with endpoint detection (EPD) was reproduced with brief discussion on secondary electron (SE) yield curve. Comprehensive understanding of ion-matter interactions would facilitate deployment of PFIB in silicon die delayering as semiconductor industry moves into the angstrom era.

articleTitle: EBSD Method for Measuring Wafer Off-cut Angle
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: Crystal orientation and off-cut angle are critical parameters in semiconductor wafer manufacturing, impacting epitaxial layer quality and device performance. This paper presents a novel method utilizing Electron Backscatter Diffraction (EBSD) to measure the orientation and off-cut angle of semiconductor wafers, providing a simpler, faster, and more efficient alternative to X-ray Diffraction (XRD). The EBSD method involves calibrating the SEM stage, collecting EBSD data, and analyzing the data based on pole figures. Three commercial (001) oriented GaAs wafers with different nominal off-cut angles of 6°, 14°, and 15° respectively were studied using this method. The measured results by EBSD are 5.97°, 14.01° and 15.06°, demonstrating close agreement between EBSD measurements and nominal values. Results indicate an average angular precision of 0.04° and excellent repeatability. Compared to XRD, EBSD offers advantages in sample alignment, data acquisition speed, and data processing simplicity, making it a valuable complement to traditional XRD techniques in semiconductor manufacturing quality assurance.

articleTitle: Increasing chain diagnosis resolution in the age of backside power
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: Scan chain diagnosis has long been used to identify manufacturing defects and yield issues in early ramp. Identifying and eliminating these yield issues quickly and efficiently are required to ensure business success of a product. Root causing defect mechanisms that produce yield loss require a combination of fault isolation and failure analysis. The advent of new technologies, like backside power, in advanced process nodes have made fault isolation extremely challenging. In this paper, we present results from three new software-based technologies that provide accurate localization to enable efficient failure analysis of both front-end of line and back-end of line defects. Additionally, these technologies can alleviate the pressure on fault isolation for front-end of line defects and provide reduced area for back-end of line defects for Physical Failure Analysis (PFA).

articleTitle: Scalable Production of Two-Dimensional Materials and Its Reliable Resistive Switching
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: Two-dimensional materials (2DM) have attracted much attention and been widely utilized in the field of optoelectronics because of their superior optical properties, wide bandgaps, and intrinsic flexibility. However, preparing large-area 2DM films is one of the main challenges in their development in the industry. In this work, we developed a universal and facile phase-interface transfer method for the preparation of large-area and high-quality 2DM films (including graphene oxides (GO), MXene) with Janus structure, which are transferred on target substrates and constructed Ag/Janus-2DM/ITO/PET flexible memristors. The results indicate that Janus-2DM based memristors have presented stable unipolar and bipolar resistive switching (RS) behaviors by tuning the presence of surface modifier between the active layer and top/bottom electrodes. In addition, the devices also present low switching voltages (~0.42 V) and high retention time (~3000 s), as well as reproducible RS behaviors under the bending radius of 5 mm.

articleTitle: Characterization Analysis of Organophosphate Contamination on Aluminum Pad
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: This study was a special case of contamination deposited on the surface of aluminum pad. In the beginning, dried water droplet-like deposits were found on aluminum pad surface, and these deposits were distributed around the periphery of the aluminum pad frame. The Optical Microscope (OM) and Scanning Electron Microscope (SEM) were first used to inspect these contamination/corrosion products, then the interface between the contamination/deposit and aluminum metal was checked by cross-sectional Transmission Electron Microscope (TEM). The TEM analysis indicated this case was a contamination deposited on Al pad surface, not a corrosion case. At the same time, the composition of the contamination deposit was examined by Energy Dispersive X-ray Spectrometer (EDS) and Auger Electron Spectroscope (AES) analysis. It was found that the deposits contain Phosphorus (P), Potassium (K), Sodium (Na), Carbon (C) and Oxygen (O) elements, and no corrosive fluorine (F) element was found. Raman spectroscopy was used to identify the chemical bonding of deposit. Moreover, the deposit was also analyzed by TOF-SIMS, and the results also indicated the deposit contained potassium, phosphorus, oxygen and carbon elements as EDS results shown, and these results concluded this case was a novel case of organophosphate contamination of aluminum pad. BG tape that directly contacted with the wafers surface in BGBM (Backside Grinding and Backside Metallization) process would not induce this contamination event; the organic Airborne Molecular Contamination (oAMC) did that. The reaction mechanism of this event should be related to the hydrogen bonding on the surface of the aluminum pad. The active mechanism was proposed.

articleTitle: The Application of Time-Domain Reflectometry (TDR) Technique in Characterizing Solder Ball Failure and Accumulated Damage in SiP Device
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: Compared to traditional packaging, System-in-Package (SiP) devices have advantages such as high integration density, short development cycle, and lower manufacturing costs. However, as the packaging density increases and the number of stacked layers grows, the occurrence of SiP device failures caused by Solder balls has become more frequent. Currently, there is a lack of specialized non-destructive testing methods for SiP device solder balls. This paper proposed a non-destructive testing technique based on Time-Domain (TDR) technology, which successfully located the failed Solder balls. Moreover, the TDR non-destructive testing technique can be used to monitor the accumulated damage of solder balls in SiP devices, providing a reference for characterizing the degradation of Solder ball during operating.

articleTitle: Unsupervised Domain Adaptation with Pseudo Shape Supervision for IC Image Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: Deep learning (DL) techniques have achieved excellent results for IC image segmentation, a critical task in hardware assurance, but they require a large amount of labeled training data to perform well. Due to the domain shift problem of DL techniques, the data collection and data labeling process has to be repeated on new IC image datasets which is extremely time-consuming. Domain adaptation is a promising approach that aims to tackle the domain shift problem by implementing models that can be trained on an existing source dataset and then applied to a new target dataset effectively. However, the reported domain adaptation techniques do not fully utilize the unlabeled images for training or are prone to model collapse when training on unlabeled images. To address these challenges, we propose pseudo shape supervision (PSS), a domain adaptation framework for IC image segmentation that effectively leverages unlabeled target images for training whilst avoiding model collapse. Within our PSS, we propose a novel shape consistency loss for supervision on unlabeled images, by utilizing weak pseudo-labels that are generated by thresholding. Cross domain mixing is performed between the unlabeled target images and the synthetic images to reduce the domain gap. Our experimental results demonstrate that our proposed PSS outperforms the reported techniques on IC image datasets and our ablation studies show the importance of our novel shape consistency loss.

articleTitle: Dopant Analysis of SiC MOSFET with Scanning Probe Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: Silicon carbide metal oxide semiconductor field effect transistor (MOSFET) has the advantages of high frequency, high withstand voltage, high efficiency, etc., thus has received widespread attention in recent years. As SiC MOSFET devices evolve, it becomes increasingly important to accurately predict the device's electrical performance. To achieve this, the doping concentration and profile of the MOSFET active region must be monitored at the nanometer scale. Scanning Probe Microscopy (SPM) technology is crucial in semiconductor failure analysis, providing high-resolution imaging and surface characterization to identify defects caused by abnormal doping. Scanning capacitance microscopy (SCM), scanning diffusion resistance microscopy (SSRM) and scanning microwave impedance microscopy (sMIM) derived from Atomic Force Microscopy (AFM) have become the current mainstream methods for two-dimensional doping characterization since they can provide high-resolution doping information efficiently and directly. In this article, we characterized the doping concentration and type, as well as the profile of the SiC MOSFET by SCM, SSRM and sMIM, through systematic experiments. And the performance of the three technologies in SiC MOSFET characterization was compared. In addition, based on the problems existing in current characterization methods, we also conducted a series of experiments to overcome or eliminate their shortcomings, which provides an important reference for the characterization of SiC MOSFETs in the future. Appropriate methods can be selected according to different purposes and needs.

articleTitle: Benchmarking BTI Reliability in Scaled FETs with TMD Channels via Predictive Modeling
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: Transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) offer excellent opportunities to continue scaling of modern electronics following Moore's law. However, the use of TMD channels together with high-k 3D oxides which was selected by the industry as the main path for FAB integration of these new devices may result in severe reliability limitations. To get more insight into this problem, here we perform predictive modeling of bias-temperature instabilities (BTI) in FETs with different TMD channels. Our findings suggest that in the ideal case MoSe2 n-FETs as well as MoS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> and MoSe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> p-FETs could fully satisfy 30mV per 10 years BTI failure criteria. Nevertheless, in reality, the use of thin highly amorphous, and thus defective SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> seed layers to grow high-k oxides like HfO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> on TMDs may still severely degrade the reliability of TMD FETs. Still our results show that the use of MoSe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> may be attractive for both n- and p-FETs as considerably improved bias stability can be achieved at positive and negative gate voltages.

articleTitle: A novel SCF H2O process increasing Hf02 MOSCAP reliability
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: The study investigated the reliability of ALD-HfO2 dielectric MOSCAP after H2 annealing, SCF H2, and SCF H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O treatments. Experimental results showed that, after SCF H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O treatment, D<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">it</inf> decreased and reliability under RTA process at 400°C improved. This phenomenon may be attributed to the stronger dissociation of Si-OH bonds compared to Si-H bonds. The NBTI experiment further confirmed the model. In addition, comparing the CET changes after the three process conditions, it can be confirmed that there is no additional CET contribution due to water after SCF H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O treatment. Finally, XPS analysis was used to confirm that the proportion of Si-OH bonds of device with the SCF H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O treatment increased at the Si/SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> interface. Based on the experimental results, it is suggested that SCF H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O is advantageous for applications in advanced process MOSFET defect passivation, reducing interface defects, enhancing reliability, and prolonging chip lifetime.

articleTitle: The Effect of the P-Substrate Connection on the HBM Robustness of P-type ESD Device
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: Although the p-substrate connection of p-type ESD device does not have any impact on the device's It2 while connecting the p-substrate to the ground degrades the human-body model (HBM) robustness of the device significantly. From the experiment results, adding N-type buried layer (NBL) to p-type ESD device can have the device HBM robustness invariant to the p-substrate connection. Based on the T-CAD simulations, the effect of the p-substrate connection on the HBM robustness of p-type ESD device is revealed in this paper. As HBM raises up the potential of the whole region of p-type ESD device after the onset of zapping for a while and then the high potential region of the device decreases with decreasing HBM current if the p-substrate is grounded, resulting in the current crowding. On the contrary, the high potential region of p-type ESD device does not decrease with decreasing HBM current if the p-substrate is floating or NBL is added to the device, resulting in the uniform current distribution.

articleTitle: Degradation Mechanism of Threshold Voltage of 1.2-kV Planar-Gate SiC MOSFETs Under the Combined Action of Surge Current and HTGB Stress
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: This paper investigates the degradation mechanism of threshold voltage (V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</inf>) of 1.2-kV planargate SiC MOSFETs under surge current and high temperature gate bias (HTGB) cross-stress. By measuring and comparing the electrical parameters of the device under test (DUT), we analyzed the drift mechanism of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V$</tex> <inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</inf> of DUT under cross-stress. Compared with HTGB stress, DUT under cross-stress has lower <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V$</tex> <inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</inf> drift. We investigated the trap characteristics of DUT under cross-stress using low-frequency noise (LFN) technology. The introduced surge current stress can improve the interface quality of degraded DUT. The results may provide useful guidance for the design and long-term application of SiC MOSFETs.

articleTitle: Power Amplifier Die Moisture Ingress Point Detection Using Nano-Fluorescent Dye Penetration Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: In wafer fabrication, silicon nitride (Si3N4) layer is widely used in semiconductor devices as a passivation layer to prevent moisture ingress into the die that would cause problems like delamination, corrosion and metal migration, etc. In this study, a Power Amplifier (PA) die which is passivated with a layer of Si3N4 was found to have delamination, corrosion, and metal migration after uHAST 96hrs that caused Icc leakage failure. It is suspected that the failures were caused by moisture invasion. However, traditional FA techniques such as Scanning Acoustic Microscopy (C-SAM) and X-Ray inspection cannot detect any defect of the die due to their detection limit. To solve the above challenges, Nano-Fluorescent dye penetration test was performed to determine the possible moisture ingress point that resulted in the delamination, corrosion, and metal corrosion in the PA die. After florescent liquid soaking, the die was inspected under fluorescent microscope. Sign of fluorescent residues were observed on the PA die which could be the possible moisture ingress point. Focused Ion Beam (FIB) cross sections were performed to verify the fluorescent finding. It is found that Si3N4 crack and Benzocyclobutene (BCB) delamination under the fluorescent residues that allowed the moisture ingress into the die and caused the delamination, corrosion and metal migration that resulted in the Icc leakage failure. This work shows that Nano-Fluorescent dye method is a useful and yet economical FA technique to detect surface defect of the passivation layer of a die.

articleTitle: Delamination Failure Analysis on FCBGA Package with Heat Spreader
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: With continuous increase in computing demand in almost all semiconductor field, Flip-chip ball grid array (FCBGA) packages are widely used. Most of failure analysis on FCBGA were focused on the thermal performance and reliability of thermal interface materials (TIM) in FCBGA package. In this study, we focused on the delamination failure of the FCBGA package with heat spreader after high temperature operating life (HTOL) test. Combined X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) and Time-of-flight secondary ion mass spectrometry (TOFSIMS) technique has been found to be an effective method for surface contamination analysis on FCBGA packages. The results revealed that there is indeed a thin siloxane related contamination on top surface of the failed heat spreader, causing the delamination failure after HTOL test. In addition, it is suggested that this failure may be reworkable by applying Ar/O2 plasma cleaning. Further verification is in progress.

articleTitle: Fault localization of Cold-temperature Scan failures by integrating Soft Defect Localization and Electro-Optical Probing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: Scan testing has been the main method for testing in the semiconductor industry due to its extremely high test coverage and high reliability in determining the suspected region of failure. Scan test failures typically fail solidly across voltage, frequency, and temperature. However, there are scan failures that would only fail at cold temperatures and are classified as temperature-dependent scan failures. Electro-Optical Probing (EOP) analysis is usually performed when the part fails to observe abnormal transistor switching activity. However, The main challenge behind cold temperature scan failures is the inability to perform EOP at very cold temperatures mainly due to tool limitations with conventional tool setup. This paper will further discuss a new approach by performing EOP at room temperature on three different types of scan failures (Stuck-at, Time-delay, and Chain) that would still yield tangible fault isolation results by referencing the Soft Defect Localization (SDL) hotspot performed at cold temperature.

articleTitle: Combining Electrical Fault Isolation and Physical Failure Analysis Inside an SEM to Locate and Characterize Gate Leakages on a 3 nm Device
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: This work employs an easy-to-use method to quickly find and characterize leakage currents on a semiconductor sample by combining electrical fault isolation and physical failure analysis. By using a simple add-on for a probing system's tip holders, a prober is transformed into a scanning device that measures currents through a sample's surface and visualizes the currents in a 2D color map that can be superimposed onto the SE image. As a case study, an area of 1.5 μm x 1.5 μm of a 3 nm device was scanned while the current through the contacts was measured and visualized with Current Imaging (CI) and gate currents were characterized. One leaking gate could be identified and the position of the failure localized using Electron Beam Induced Resistance CHange (EBIRCH) imaging. This technique also avoids any damage caused by electron beam irradiation as the beam can be switched off during scanning.

articleTitle: Revisiting 3D X-ray for Board Level FA to In-line Metrology of Wafer Level Integration
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: While 3D X-ray Tools or X-ray Microscopes (XRM) have been the traditional nondestructive imaging tools in Failure Analysis (FA) labs, they normally involve smaller packages or small sections cut out of a package or PCB if high resolution better than 1 um is desired. They are seldom used for intact board level FA nor is a tool of choice for inline metrology for defect inspection in wafer level integration. As sample size increases to several cm, such as 2.SD/3D Packages, Multi Chiplet Modules (MCM), PCBs or a 300 mm wafer, high resolution (< 1 um) imaging is not practical nor in many cases achievable. The acquisition time takes too long (typically hours); images are noisy and are filled with beam hardening artifacts (with bands and streaks). In this paper we will revisit the use of X-rays for high resolution (sub-micron) board level FA and in line metrology for next generation wafer level integration using a novel 3D X-ray system that can achieve sub-micron resolution on large PCBs to 300 mm wafers in as little as a few minutes to evaluate failures or defects in 3D.

articleTitle: Static Fault Isolation on Memory BIST Failure
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: Conventionally, memory bitmapping is utilized to identify the failing location in the Static Random Access Memory (SRAM) array for physical failure analysis. However, in a foundry environment, this capability may not always be available for memory BIST failure debug. In our previous publication, we have reported that photon emission microscopy (PEM) can be utilized to localize subtle short and open defects that have impacted the local or global wordline resulting in detectable emission from the pass gate transistor [5]. In this paper, we extended this study and described three case studies that illustrate additional SRAM failure modes that could potentially produce detectable hotspot using a combination of PEM and TIVA techniques for fault isolation. This would serve as a good reference to better understand the static fault isolation defect detection coverage on SRAM cell functional failure.

articleTitle: Fluorocarbon Film Deposition Using Reactive Ion Etcher and Its Application for Physical Analysis of 3D Stacking TSV, Micro Bump and Hybrid Bonding
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: Through-silicon via (TSV), micro bump, and hybrid bonding are three critical structures for three-dimensional (3D) integrated circuits (IC) stacking technology. The large-scale (~urn level) feature size will be the challenge for conventional physical analysis and the development of new techniques must be considered. During the sample preparation process in focused ion beam (FIB), a protection layer deposition is necessary to avoid the damage by subsequent ion milling, especially for samples where the region of interest (ROI) is on the surface. It consumes time and only small area is capable due to the low deposition rate in FIB. Besides, the material contrast in scanning electron microscope (SEM) images is low if only metallic precursors in FIB can be selected. Therefore, a new protection layer which is non-metallic material and can be deposited over a large area is considered. This paper investigates the possibility of fluorocarbon film deposition utilizing the reactive ion etcher (RIE) as a new option for the protection layer. The precursor trifluoromethane (CHF3) is generally used for silicon oxide etching in RIE. However, the literature indicates that it can also be used for fluorocarbon film deposition under specific process conditions. The experiment results show that the fluorocarbon film can be deposited successfully in RIE using CHF3 without oxygen (O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>). Lower radio frequency (RF) power and higher chamber pressure enhance the deposition rate. The profile can be observed by SEM images and energy dispersive spectroscopy (EDS) verified the existence of carbon and fluorine compounds on the surface. The fluorocarbon film is further applied as the protection layer on TSV, micro bump and hybrid bonding samples for subsequent FIB cross-sectional preparation. It not only saves the deposition time in FIB, but also provides high transparency for target navigation by top view and better material contrast for cross-sectional images. This study successfully develops a new technique for physical analysis in 3D stacking technology and creates a deposition function on the etching tool, which is a significant achievement in the physical and failure analysis laboratory.

articleTitle: Novel Rapid and Deposition-Free Strategy for FIB Cross-Section Preparation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: In this work a novel focused ion beam (FIB) cross-section preparation method of “flying cube” is presented, which allows time savings of 60-85% of the time required for cross-section preparation compared to the standard processes applied so far. Furthermore, it enables high-quality crosssections even for samples with thick non-conductive or poorly conductive layers (e.g., photoresist, PMMA or SiO2) and samples with cavities or pronounced topographies. Thereby it gets along with no deposition of impurities on the wafer surface other than the sputtered and redeposited material. Due to the great flexibility, it is possible to extend the field of application beyond the field of electronics and semiconductors.

articleTitle: The Applications of Simulation and Artificial Intelligence in Advanced Packaging
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: Advanced Packaging enables the heterogenous integration of chiplets with die embedding and die stacking techniques, and provides maximum device performance with much faster product development cycle. However, as the 2.5D and 3D packages are getting more and more complicated, it is very challenging to ramp the yield and assure the reliability of new products within the short timeline, using conventional methods. Artificial Intelligence (AI) assisted design co-optimization, manufactory process simulation and monitoring, yield enhancement, reliability assurance, and failure mode prediction, which are developed for Si fabrication, could be employed to shorten the advanced packaging development cycle. This paper summarizes the current status for the various applications of simulation and AI in advanced packaging. Further development trends are highlighted with the goal of providing a holistic and robust virtual representation, or digital twin, for advanced packaging.

articleTitle: Improved Positive Bias Temperature Instability of n-type Vertical C-Shaped-Channel Nanosheet FET by Forming Gas Annealing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: In this article, the influence of Forming Gas Annealing (FGA) on the Positive Bias Temperature Instability (PBTI) characteristics of n-vertical C-shaped-channel nanosheet FET (n-VCNFET) is studied. The experimental results show that the extra FGA can significantly suppress both the initial and generated interface traps in PBTI. Moreover, in ultra-fast PBTI the pre-existing trap and total trap of VCNFET due to FGA decreases by 35% and 31%, respectively. The energy level of the oxide trap under PBTI and recovery doesn't change, in other words, the FGA induces the oxide trap density of the devices to decrease by 36% at 125°C and 1.4V Vov. The optimization effect of FGA annealing has been further confirmed from the perspective of trap generation. It provides a guideline for the PBTI improvement of VCNFET in trap scopes.

articleTitle: Investigating Reliability Issues in Multi-Layered STT-MRAM with Synthetic Antiferromagnets
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: In exploring the reliability issues of multi-layered STT-MRAM, particularly with synthetic antiferromagnets, our research delves into the complexities of magnetization dynamics. We leverage the spin drift-diffusion model to investigate the intricacies of the back-hopping effect which leads to undesired switching in the device's layers. This phenomenon is notably magnified as devices become smaller, aiming for higher memory density but at the cost of data integrity. Our focus extends to the nuanced role of interface exchange coupling in multilayered configurations, illustrating its pivotal influence on the magnetic interactions and stability within these advanced spintronic devices. By examining how the non-magnetic layers mediate exchange coupling and impact the magnetic coherence between ferromagnetic layers, we gain crucial insights into the mechanisms driving magnetic stability and domain wall behaviors. This comprehensive approach, encompassing both charge and spin currents, offers a comprehensive view of MRAM dynamics and underscores the importance of fine-tuning exchange coupling for enhanced device performance. This kind of advancements are aimed to significantly elevate the capabilities of memory technologies, paving the way for improved data retention and faster write/read operations. Our findings represent a significant stride in advancing high-capacity and high-efficiency memory solutions.

articleTitle: ESD and Latch-Up Design Verification Challenges in Packaged Parts and Modules
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: ESD and latch-up stress testing to meet industry standards is performed on packaged parts and modules. However, ESD and latch-up design verification has been historically done on die / silicon database. In case of inadequate protection, ESD and latch-up damage occurs on silicon. However, package and module configurations play a significant role. Packages and modules based on the same silicon die can have very different ESD and latch-up protection levels. In this paper we review package and module properties impacting ESD and latch-up protection. These properties include package and module size, capacitance, package wire connectivity and inductance. We discuss ESD and latch-up EDA challenges in packaged parts and modules. We propose a new verification flow to access ESD and latch-up on package and module levels as well as outline the implementation steps.

articleTitle: Degradation of Off-State Performance and Its Reliability of NMOS with Deep N Well Induced by Plasma Charging
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: Deep N well (DNW) can provide good noise isolation and is widely used in RF circuits. However, it is usually susceptible to plasma charging during manufacturing. This study presents the off-state drain leakage, rather than gate leakage that is traditionally focused on, can be much deteriorated in DNW devices in comparison with those without DNW, even if the antenna ratio of the former is much smaller. A new plasma-induced damage (PID) mechanism is proposed which concerns well injection of hot plasma charges during manufacturing as a result of DNW isolation, followed by generation of much more precursors of both donor-type and acceptor-type interfacial states. It also results in larger degradation of the on-state performance, as well as unusual pinning or quick increasing of the off-state leakage in DNW devices under HCI stress. The research may contribute to full understanding and effective detection of the impact of PID on the performance and reliability of DNW devices and facilitate secure usage of them.

articleTitle: Influence of N2 Gas Flow on the Reliability of Indium Zinc Oxide Thin-Film Transistors
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: This study investigates the effects of different nitrogen (N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) gas flow rates on the back-channel doping of indium zinc oxide (IZO) thin-film transistors (TFTs), focusing on the impact on device performance and stability. By introducing different N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> flow rates into the back-channel, the device performance, negative bias stress reliability, and negative bias illumination stress reliability are respectively examined. The results confirm that introducing an appropriate amount of nitrogen into the back-channel could enhance device performance and reliability. N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, acting as a substitute for oxygen, efficiently infiltrates oxygen vacancies within the oxygen-rich film, effectively suppressing the formation of oxygen vacancies and thereby enhancing the stability of a-IZO TFTs. This research contributes to understanding the potential of N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> doping as a promising avenue for improving the reliability of MO TFTs.

articleTitle: Failure analysis of ASIC controller integrated in embedded flash memory package under biased-HAST reliability failure
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: The emergence of embedded flash memory specifically for 3D NAND technology represents a significant advancement in data storage for electronic devices. This innovative approach offers a compelling combination of compactness, improved operational efficiency, and superior performance across diverse applications. However, understanding and mitigating potential failure mechanisms is critical to ensure device reliability and prevent future malfunctions. This study investigates the characterization of electrical overstress (EOS) within the application-specific integrated circuit (ASIC) controller for embedded flash memory utilizing 3D NAND technology. The investigation employs a biased high accelerated stress test (Biased-HAST) with a controlled variation of bias conditions and stress durations to study on the product reliability. The characterization of defect within the ASIC controller using Biased-HAST provides valuable insights for improving device reliability and ensuring long-term functionality. By understanding these failure mechanisms, manufacturers can implement preventative measures and extend the lifespan of these advanced storage devices.

articleTitle: Enhancing Performance and Reliability of MISGaN HEMT by Advanced Supercritical Fluid Nitridation Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: In this study, an advanced supercritical fluid nitridation (SCF-N) treatment is employed to enhance the electrical properties and reliability of GaN metal-insulatorsemiconductor high electron mobility transistors (MISHEMTs). According to electrical measurements, the treated devices exhibit higher ON-state current, lower gate leakage current, a larger ON/OFF ratio, and reduced OFF-state leakage under high drain bias and temperature. Additionally, the threshold voltage (V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">TH</inf>) of the device remains unchanged after treatment. This provides significant evidence that SCFN effectively eliminates material vacancy defects and interface defects between AlGaN and the insulator. The suppression of current collapse is also confirmed through dynamic Ron measurements. High temperature reverse bias stress (HTRB) testing further validates the passivation of defects by SCF-N, leading to improved reliability. Consequently, the SCF-N technique demonstrates great potential for enhancing power devices, paving the way for their effective and practical application in the future.

articleTitle: Study on Different Failure Mechanisms of MOSFET Caused by Different Oxide Defects in 14nm FinFET IC
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: With the application of FinFET technology, especially as FinFET technology nodes reach 14nm and beyond, we will see more and more front-end-of-line (FEOL) defects at the transistor level, rather than back-end-of-line (BEOL) interconnection defects. These minor defects often have a significant impact on the yield and reliability of the final chipsets. This paper presents two different types of FEOL defects in 14nm FINFET technology. (Finding the approximate location by EFA, further fault isolation down to MOSFET by nanoprobe, finding the physical defect by TEM analysis). Both types of FEOL defects result in leakage of MOSFETs. We studied the different failure mechanisms and the possible mechanism of formation. Finally, it was concluded that both of them were probably caused by the oxide defect in different steps of the FEOL process. One NMOS leakage case was gate leakage, and the failure mechanism was dielectric-breakdown-induced epitaxy (DBIE), which may be caused by an Oxide bottom interface layer (BIL) defect. Another PMOS leakage case was mainly Drain and Source short, and the failure mechanism was the Ge bridge defect, which may be caused by the Oxide Etch Stop Layer (ESL) defect going through a series of subsequent process steps. It provided evidence for the fab process, and yield-quality improvement in 14nm FinFET. Also, it was instructive and meaningful to the FinFET failure analysis.

articleTitle: High Resolution CT Cross Section Observation Using Vertical Oblique CT Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: With the advent of three-dimensional stacking in semiconductor packages, the role of X-ray CT in non-destructive failure analysis has become increasingly critical. Additionally, as the internal structures of packages, such as bumps and VIAs, become finer, the demand for higher resolution in X-ray CT continues to grow. However, conventional X-ray CT systems require the sample to be rotated perpendicularly to the X-ray optical axis. This necessitates maintaining a certain distance between the sample and the X-ray source, which precludes high magnification imaging. To address this issue, Oblique CT technology was developed in the early 2000s and has since become prevalent in the semiconductor industry. Oblique CT allows for significantly higher CT imaging magnification compared to conventional CT, enabling CT scans with submicron resolution even for large packages. However, Oblique CT has the disadvantage of not being able to obtain accurate vertical slice images. In our efforts to overcome this limitation as an X-ray equipment manufacturer, we have devised a new imaging technique called Vertical Oblique CT. In this paper, we will first clarify the differences between conventional CT and Oblique CT, and then introduce the new imaging technique called Vertical Oblique CT.

articleTitle: Distribution of HCD-induced Interface Trap in nano-scale Si n-FinFET due to Corner Effect
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: In this paper, in order to understand the interface trap distribution along channel induced by Hot Carrier Degradation (HCD) of nano-scale Si n-FinFETs, both Bias Temperature Instability (BTI) and HCD of n-FinFETs are compared. Under BTI stress, the short-channel n-FinFET is influenced by both corner passivation effects and a larger corner electric field. Interface traps exhibit a lower density in the short-channel device at lower stress voltages, but surpass it at higher stress voltages. During HCD stress, the degradation process in short-channel devices is predominantly dominated by a larger lateral electric field, resulting in significantly fewer interface traps. Moreover, interface traps in short-channel devices no longer accumulate near the drain side, as observed in long-channel devices, but extend towards the source, distributed across the entire channel.

articleTitle: Case Study of High-Temperature Induced Slip Defect Causing Overlay Issue
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: Lots of processes in Si device fabrication involve high-temperature surroundings of up to 1000°C, such as the epitaxial growth of the Si epi layer. This high-temperature process will be the main reason that causes Si-related defects such as Si dislocation or slip defect. This defect may create problems for subsequent wafer fabrication processes and in severe cases may lead to device failure. A case study of high temperature-induced slip defects was presented and discussed in this paper. Confirmation of slip defect on affected wafer with failure analysis finding helped to identify the root cause of the issue. Hence, effective corrective action can be implemented to prevent similar issues from reoccurrence.

articleTitle: Nano-probing Technique for Flip-Flop Circuit with Diffusion Defect
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: Electron Beam Absorbed Current (EBAC) is an omnipresent technique in nano-probing field commonly utilized for local electrical fault isolation at die level. It complements the conventional global electrical fault isolation techniques of photon and thermal emission analyses as well as OBIRCH (Optical Beam Induced Resistance Change) analysis. In this paper, we develop an inclusive procedure for analyzing flip-flop circuits in memory devices impaired with read functional failures, which has not been reported in any other literature. We also elaborate on deep-dive physical analysis at the isolated defective sites to reveal subtle Silicon diffusion defects which have caused the read failures.

articleTitle: TOF-SIMS Analytical Method for Gate Oxide Breakdown Voltage Shift Failure
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: Traditional failure analysis for gate oxide (GOX) breakdown voltage (BV) shift involves electrical fault isolation of the defect and wright etch to discriminate plasma induced defects or contamination. To further nail down the root cause of the contamination, secondary ion mass spectrometry (SIMS) is proposed due to its superior detection sensitivity at ppm or ppb level and superior mass resolution to determine the foreign elements or materials unambiguously. In this paper, a PMOS device failure was found to be gate oxide breakdown voltage shifted down. Time-of-Flight (TOF) -SIMS depth profile is thus used for the all-elements search mode analysis to figure out the contamination, which is consistent with the inline process commonality analysis results.

articleTitle: Analysis of Different Impact of LDD Missing and Silicide Missing Defects on MOSFET Characteristic
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: Metal-oxide-semiconductor field-effect transistor (MOSFET) is regarded as a most important modern electronic semiconductor device that is widely used in automobile chips. Nanoprobing analysis is considered to be an effective methodology to detect and localize lightly doped drain (LDD) missing and Ni- silicide missing defects hidden in failed MOSFET. It reveals that above two structural defects exhibit different impact on MOSFET transfer characteristic, so we offer analysts idea to select an optimal physical analysis solution especially critical for failure analysis (FA) success of end-user returned single sample. Current-voltage (I-V) characteristic shows that LDD missing defect causes 50-fold to around 100-fold on-state current drop while silicide missing defect just generates current decrease by about 50-fold or less. In addition, LDD missing defect does not affect junction I-V characteristic. In contrast, silicide missing defect increases drain (source) contact resistance. Silicide missing increases series resistance at W-Si interface while LDD missing brings severe hot electron effect to device. Considering physical analytical methods, wet chemical stain is a preferred technique to localize LDD missing site whereas the silicide missing place contained in a lamella is identified by transmission electron microscope (TEM). In conclusion, nanoprobing analysis combined with right physical analysis techniques correlates two failure mechanisms with MOSFET low on-state current anomaly theoretically and experimentally. The study enables wafer fabs to find out the root cause of subtle defects in the front-end-of-line (FEOL) process.

articleTitle: Augmenting Metrology: A Framework for Interactive 3D Data Visualization and Contextual Analysis in Semiconductor Manufacturing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: This work presents the first application of an Augmented Reality (AR) and Virtual Reality (VR) environment for the navigation and analysis of complex 3D metrology datasets in chip manufacturing and debugging. Our platform overcomes the limitations of traditional 2D data visualization by facilitating seamless access, navigation, and co-registration of multi-modal datasets acquired through tomographic scanning probe microscopy, 3D rendering software, and finite element simulations. Our goal is to demonstrate the functionality and advantages of such a platform for the analysis of complex 3D datasets, typically generated during the process of failure analysis (FA). First, we describe our platform with details for the access and navigation of existing datasets. Second, we offer the seamless presentation of various co-registered datasets acquired by a combination of tomographic scanning probe microscopy, multiple FA techniques, and 3D finite elements software simulations. Our first-person perspective enables the enhancement of data navigation for each of these tasks. For example, with the simultaneous observation of static 2D information about the sample under study e.g., graphic data stream (GDS) floorplan or scanning electron microscopy (SEM), while offering 3D interactive inspection of an inherently tomographic dataset.

articleTitle: Scanning-TEM EDX Elemental Mapping Study and Observations in Semiconductor Device Failure Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: Scanning-TEM EDX mapping has become a mainstream analytical technique in semiconductor device failure analysis as it offers fast elemental identification with high spatial resolution. This is made possible with the technological advancement in the silicon drift detectors (SDD) which replaces conventional lithium-drifted silicon Si (Li) detectors. The higher X-ray count rate from SDDs significantly reduces EDX mapping collection time while improving the sensitivity of low atomic weight elements. In this paper, we present some common challenges that may happen during EDX analysis. These case studies discuss problems with peak overlapping, signal absorption, and beam-sensitive material. Through the findings and observations of this study, we proposed strategies that can be used to achieve better and more reliable EDX mapping results.

articleTitle: Optimization of Cathodoluminescence from GaN Using Low-Voltage SEM
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: GaN wafers, which are compound semiconductors with large band gaps, are integral components of power semiconductor devices. However, it is difficult to synthesize crystals without any dislocation, and research on crystal growth is still ongoing. In particular, there is an urgent need to synthesize high-quality GaN wafers with few dislocation defects for use in power semiconductor devices, and methods for analyzing these defects are also being studied. Photoluminescence (PL) analysis is generally used to analyze dislocation defects in compound semiconductors such as GaN. However, the spatial resolution of the PL method is in the order of several hundred nanometers, making it difficult to find tiny dislocation defects with nano-meter level in compound semiconductors. The cross-sectioning is also crucial for failure analysis of chips. In this paper, we investigate the optimized conditions of analyzing dislocation defects in compound semiconductors using different accelerating voltages with low voltage scanning electron microscope (SEM)-cathodoluminescence (CL) including sample cross-sectioning.

articleTitle: Identification of Recovering Package Leakage Failure Mode Via Novel Comprehensive Failure Analysis Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: The packaging of semiconductors significantly impacts their performance, especially with the current emphasis on energy-saving applications. Increasing package complexity has led to issues such as leakage. Therefore, failure analysis (FA) is crucial in identifying the actual root cause of these failures. Device recovery issues have been rising, correlating directly with advancements in new process technologies and packaging methods. This paper introduces a novel FA methodology that combines electrical characteristic analysis, precise package fault isolation, mechanical cross-sectioning, and Focused Ion Beam (FIB) techniques. This integrated approach helps resolve failure recovery issues and efficiently identify the root causes of failure mechanisms. Without proper FA procedures for recoverable package leakages, critical evidence might be missed, leading to inaccurate FA results or conclusions and a high chance of recurring failures. The proposed methodology begins with electrical characterization to identify anomalies, followed by precise fault isolation to pinpoint the fault. Mechanical cross-sectioning or FIB allows for a detailed examination of the package layers. By integrating these techniques, our methodology provides a comprehensive view of the failure mechanism, ensuring no potential cause is overlooked. In summary, this work presents a comprehensive FA methodology that enhances the identification of device failure mechanisms. As a result, package recovery issues are addressed effectively, providing the production team with precise insights into the failure mechanisms and facilitating accurate investigations. This methodology resolves immediate recovery issues and contributes to long-term improvements in semiconductor packaging and performance.

articleTitle: Fault Localization on ICs by Function Based OBIRCH Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: OBIRCH is commonly utilized in failure analysis of integrated circuit as an electrical fault analysis method, it's based on static electrical test, mainly anomaly from I-V characteristics curve. For functional failures, OBIRCH is supposed to be limited since the bias of function failures is complicated, it's hard to find a leakage current path by single OBIRCH source. Function based OBIRCH is proposed to solve functional failures and soft defects, the IC is electrically biased by external power source, I/O signal and embedded source of OBIRCH. The external source and I/O signal provide a testable leakage path, and the leakage is detected by OBIRCH amplifier. Results demonstrate function based OBIRCH is efficient in fault localization of oxide defects or breakdown, even soft defect sensitive to temperature.

articleTitle: Failure Analysis of a Bus Circuit Under Slow Power-on Induced by Process Deviation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: Failure analysis of a bus circuit under slow power-on induced by process deviation. A bus circuit fails with slow power-on at low temperature. The failure reason of the bus circuit is the reference source of the transmitter is invalid, which is resulted in the offset of the amplifier of the reference source. The failure mechanism of the bus circuit is analyzed. The offset of the amplifier of the reference source is resulted in the process deviation of the reference source. If the power-on time of the bus circuit is long, the diode of the triode of the reference source is not open, resulting in failure of the reference source. To avoid this failure, the increased test with longer power-on time is proposed.

articleTitle: Case Study: Failure Analysis of Thin Quad Flat Pack Package (TQFP) IC
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: This article describes systematic analysis of failure occurred in a Thin Quad Flat Pack Package (TQFP) integrated circuit. The electrical testing suggested that the device failure occurred inside of the device package. The sample was analyzed through Non-Destructive techniques of X-Ray imaging and Scanning Acoustic Microscope (SAM) to get insight into the internal structure and integrity of the sample in order to identify any anomalies. Even though the Nondestructive testing exhibited some early signs of the failure but was not enough for a conclusion. Subsequently, decapsulation of the sample was exercised to examine the internal structure of the die to unveil the crucial insights into the origin of problem. A specialized resistive (constant voltage) micro-probing was opted and carried out at pad level of the die which not only identified the internal circuit issues but also revealed the associated impact of the chemicals i.e., sulfuric and nitric acid on the die, introducing further layer of complexity in failure analysis methodologies. This comprehensive study provided valuable understanding of optimized methodologies for enhancing failure analysis process and highlighted the importance of mitigating the potential risks associated with the selection of chemical procedures in semiconductor investigations.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Influence of Pin Position on CDM Peak Current Based on 2.5D and 2D Packaging
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: The trend and principle for the variation of Charged Device Model(CDM) peak current of IO and PG pins with pin position in 2.5D CoWoS(50 × 50mm) and 2D FCBGA(45 × 45mm) packaging are analyzed in this work. Pin position has an important effect on the CDM peak current, the closer to the packaging center, the higher peak current of CDM. Moreover, the peak current of the CDM depends on the total charge in the first CDM pulse(Q) and full width at half maximum time of the first CDM pulse(Td), and the trend of CDM peak current with pin position is primarily influenced by parasitic resistance for 10(InputOutput) pins and capacitance for PG(Power and Ground) pins. Furthermore, the CDM peak current of the PG pin is generally higher than that of the IO pin, as the discharge time of the IO pin is much longer than that of the PG pin, which further indicates that the parasitic resistance of the IO pin is larger than that of the PG pin. Therefore, the influence of the pin position should be considered when designing ESD protection circuits to avoid CDM-related failures caused by ESD underdesign.

articleTitle: Optical-based defect Inspection Techniques for SiC Wafers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: Silicon carbide (SiC) has been recognized as a wide band gap semiconductor since 1991, making it an ideal material for high-temperature operation and high-power applications. Furthermore, SiC exhibits exceptional thermal conductivity and possesses a significantly higher breakdown electric-field strength. It has been demonstrated that the performance of SiC devices is significantly influenced by the presence of detrimental defects, which are formed during the crystal growth process. The non-destructive defect inspection techniques capable of identifying and locating defects have emerged as an indispensable requirement within the manufacturing process. In this work, we present a comprehensive flow of SiC defect inspection technologies such as Raman, FTIR, and CL to identify the location of defects and their impact on SiC devices.

articleTitle: Characterization of Threshold-Voltage Hysteresis and Instability in 4H-SiC Power nMOSFETs
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: The interface between silicon carbide and gate oxide has long been studied and found to contain higher interface traps.
