The higher intrinsic material defects coupled with a wide bandgap introduces a phenomenon known as hysteresis which is barely observed in silicon. According to recommendations from JEDEC, applying a pulse near the maximum gate-source voltage rating of the device prior to measurement is known to reduce the threshold voltage hysteresis. In this work, we present an innovation known as SVC that achieved a uniform distribution of hysteresis values. The study on hysteresis and BTI revealed that both phenomena are uncorrelated, and likely to have originated from different sources.

articleTitle: Investigation on Gate Etching and Stability of GaN p-FETs
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: In this work, an etching recipe whose reactive gas is BCl<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> and RF power is 15W, achieved ultra-low etching rates (600s, 45nm) and excellent surface morphology. An enhanced GaN p-FETs was successfully developed, and the impact of defects introduced by p-GaN etching on the gate reliability is reverse- engineered. The results indicate that the gate/dielectric interface exists interface states with a density of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</sup>∼10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">13</sup> cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-2</sup>eV<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>, resulting in poor gate reliability and the high-temperature operational characteristics.

articleTitle: Imaging Electronic Degradation in a Stressed GaN HEMT
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: The standard tool for high-resolution imaging of microelectronics is the transmission electron microscope (TEM), which can resolve atomic-scale features in thin cross-section samples extracted from (pristine or stressed) components. However, cross-sectioning typically leaves such a sample “dead” electronically. Even for an electronically “viable” sample, TEM is insensitive to a device's electronic structure and may be blind to the dynamics responsible for a its function and failure. Here we discuss the preparation, and in situ stressing, of a cross-section extracted from a GaN high electron-mobility transistor (HEMT) using a plasma-focused ion beam (PFIB). Scanning TEM electron beam-induced current (STEM EBIC) imaging is used to confirm the electronic viability of the sample and to reveal bias-induced electronic changes under normal operating values applied in situ. Under in situ stressing, subtle electronic defects appear in STEM EBIC prior to any physical signs of stress. After stressing to the point of failure, indicated by a sudden decrease gate-source resistance, defects form which generate intense STEM EBIC contrast under small bias, but no evidence of the defects are seen with standard TEM-based imaging.

articleTitle: Identification of Crack-Detect Failure Analysis in 16nm Finfet Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: The first purpose of crack detect test is to detect any crack detect failure. The crack detect test helps to identify the possible die failure along the die perimeter. Based on the Failure Analysis (FA) flow, the test was initially run during the verification phase to detect any failure. If the test failed, the analysis was continued with the inspection including high optical microscope inspection and backside Infra-Red inspection (IR). If the crack/die chip can be observed during the inspection, the analysis should have a route to the root cause of the failure. While if not, then FA needs to analyze the failure further. This paper will further focus on identifying crack detect FA in 16nm Finfet Technology. Crack detect circuitry not only detects the metal lines that get cracked, but it also utilizes inverter buffers to propagate a signal around the die periphery. The buffers along the die periphery could be easily probed with an Electro-Optical Probe (EOP) or Laser Voltage Probe (LVP) to isolate the failing area due to simple and bigger transistor geometry size. Inverter buffers were used to acquire EOP/LVP signals. Each device was provided with a die map with a crack-detect chain section. The purpose is to identify a die chip/crack at the edge of the die. This technical paper will focus on the challenges of failure analysis techniques used to locate the failing nets precisely. The result of Physical Failure Analysis (PFA) revealed the cause of the failure which can be designated to different root causes by signature analysis. Few case studies presented in this paper will demonstrate how the nanoprobing analysis during the PFA stage helps to isolate the defect region.

articleTitle: Applications of TOF-SIMS Ion Color Mapping Technology in Characterization of IC Al Alloys and Wafer Fabrication Cleaning Process Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: Time-of-flight secondary ion mass spectrometry (TOF-SIMS) can be used for high-end failure analysis and materials analysis and characterization. It has high sensitivity, large mass range, high detection efficiency, and full element analysis. It can be applied to compositional analysis of organic and inorganic materials of all elements and ion color imaging analysis. In this paper, two practical application examples are studied. We apply TOF-SIMS surface ion color mapping analysis technology to study Al alloy materials used in semiconductor integrated circuits and optimize cleaning processes in wafer fabrication. These two application examples demonstrated the analytical capabilities and application value of TOF-SIMS analysis technology. Moreover, in the paper, the method and chemical mechanism for optimizing cleaning processes will be studied and discussed, especially for Al oxide formation on Al metal surface during the cleaning process.

Author Keywords: Wafer Fab and Cleaning Process Optimization

articleTitle: The Characterization of CoSix spike in Silicon Substrate by Transmission Electron Microscope
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: In this work, we reported an analysis case study on CoSi<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf> spike. In order to understand the generation mechanism and root cause of CoSi<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf> spike, the detailed characterization on microstructure and composition of the CoSi<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf> are performed by transmission electron microscope, including in-situ transmission electron microscope (TEM), electron energy loss spectroscopy (EELS), and energy dispersive spectroscopy (EDS). In-situ TEM is a powerful tool to analyze the evolution of CoSi<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> silicide. It was found out that during silicidation process, the volume expansion is caused by phase change, diffusion of Co atoms as well as stress in multi-phases locations are the root cause of CoSi<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>spike generation. Finally, possible solutions were provided to avoid the CoSi<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf> spike and improve the production yield.

articleTitle: Supervised Learning Approach in Automated Defect Detection for Failure Analysis in Scanning Acoustic Microscopy
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: Scanning acoustic microscopy (SAM) is a non-destructive imaging technique commonly used in failure analysis (FA) to detect defects between the semiconductor package interfacial layers. With the relentless scaling of package interconnects it is increasingly challenging for the human eye to spot defects in an acoustic image. The paper aims to study the viability of using automated defect detection through a supervised learning approach to identify defects from an acquired dataset of acoustic images. A typical dataset of acoustic images generally suffers class imbalances with more images in the “normal” class category. Our approach tackles the dataset volume increment through the usage of image patches for training. Two pre-trained convolution neural networks (CNN) are used to distinguish the “anomaly” class image patches. The Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristics Curve (AUROC) attained a value of 0.997 with the implementation of the EfficientNet architecture.

articleTitle: Sparse Denoising Method for Chip Ultrasonic Signals Based on Dual Memory-Enhanced Deep Unfolding Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: This article proposes a sparse denoising method for ultrasonic signals based on the dual memory-enhanced deep unfolding network (DME-DUN), which aims to accurately reconstruct high-frequency ultrasonic signals in flip chip detection. To address information loss during the iterative process in deep unfolding networks, two memory enhancement mechanisms are designed, i.e., adjacent-stage and cross-stage. For adjacent-stage, the high-throughput information from the previous stage is introduced into the current stage, thus facilitating the transmission of information between adjacent stages. Additionally, the cross-stage memory enhancement mechanism is applied to promote information fusion between separated stages. This mechanism is based on Richardson extrapolation and calculates the output error between every two adjacent stages to update the sparse coefficient. Extensive experiments verify that the proposed method effectively captures weak echo features while removing noise.

articleTitle: Research on intermittent fault mechanism of bond wire under vibration and environmental shock based on simulation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: High Density Integrated circuit (HDIC) is an important component of modern electronic equipment. As a key electrical connection component, bond wire is also a weak component, which is prone to failure when subjected to vibration and environmental impact. Compared with the traditional research focusing on permanent faults, intermittent faults are rarely studied due to their variable transformation characteristics, but the existence of intermittent faults cannot be ignored. In this paper, the temperature shock and vibration simulation of the bond wire are carried out, and the relevant model is constructed according to the contact resistance theory to calculate, and the intermittent breakage and short circuit mechanism of the bond wire under vibration and environmental impact are studied. This paper provides some theoretical and technical support for the intermittent faults of high-density integrated circuits.

articleTitle: Study on the Anti-Crack Propagation Behavior of a Submicron Pore-Enriched Elastomer Composite
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: Elastomeric materials play a pivotal role in the composition of flexible sensors and actuators, garnering significant attention within the realm of flexible electronics. However, the failure reliability problem of intrinsically isotropic elastomers due to crack propagation still exists. In this work, an elastomeric composite enriched in submicron voids was fabricated by overfilling silicone rubber with small-sized carbon black (CB) particles. Different from the intrinsic silicone rubber film, the porous carbon black/silicone rubber composite exhibits unusual anti-crack propagation behavior. The dynamic evolution of the morphology at the crack tip of the composite was observed by in situ scanning electron microscopy (SEM), revealing the anisotropic transformation mechanism caused by the strain on the composite.

articleTitle: Logical Data Extraction of a STT-MRAM: Backside FIB Preparation and Conductive-AFM Measurements
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: The reading of the memory state (i.e., whether a bit is at ‘0’ or ‘1’) on an individual magnetic tunnel junction (MT J) in a commercial spin-transfer torque magnetic random access memory (STT-MRAM) is still a challenging task. This is mainly due to the nanoscale size of the memory cell. This paper proposes a probing approach, based on atomic force microscopy (AFM), aiming at monitoring the resistance value of the MT J, thereby determining its memory state. To achieve this objective, the 40 nm MRAM device must undergo preparation to establish electrical access on both sides of the MTJs. The appropriate methodology, developed in this paper, involves backside preparation, creating access to the bottom side of the MT Js through vias, and to the top side through bitlines primarily using a focused ion beam (FIB). Following the MRAM preparation process, the paper delves into MT J resistance probing using AFM in a conductive mode. Consequently, it becomes possible to measure the current flowing through the MT J s and assess their resistance. Results emphasize that ‘0’ and ‘1’ bits exhibit a resistance of 8.5 +/- 0.1 kΩ and 3.9 +/- 0.2 kΩ respectively which is in agreement with literature. This allows the first reading of a STT -MRAM.

articleTitle: Dual-Side Electrical Fault Isolation Workflow: Enhanced Defect Site Determination In Microcontroller Devices and Case Studies
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: In general, Electrical Fault Isolation (EFI) techniques such as Photon Emission Microscopy (PEM), Optical Beam Induced Resistance Change (OBIRCH), Laser-assisted Device Alteration (LADA)/Soft Defect Localization (SDL), in combination with probing activities, are critical to isolate and localize the most possible fault location prior to nanoprobing and physical analysis in the failure analysis (FA) workflow. Depending on the wafer technology complexity, EFI analysis can be performed either from the frontside of the die or the backside of the die. This paper explores the idea of combining the EFI techniques from the dual-side (frontside and backside of the die) to acquire more valuable EFI data for a concise conclusion in fault isolation followed by actual case studies discussion to demonstrate the benefit of the dual EFI methodology which pinpoint the defect region successfully.

articleTitle: Trench Oxide Interface States & BTI Reliability in IGBT Device
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: For trench-gated power devices, the interface between gate oxide and silicon substrate in the trench module is one of the key contributors to long-term device reliability performance, and this has become increasingly important when devices are scaled down to reduce power loss. Until now, there has been little reported work on trench oxide interface states and their impact on reliability performance. In this work, we have successfully characterized trench oxide interface states such as the quantification of interface trap density as well as reliability BTI study. A physical model was proposed to explain the BTI test and its impact on the entire trench module, including the sidewall and bottom of the trench.

articleTitle: Studies and Joint Application of TOF-SIMS and XPS in Material Analysis and Characterization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: In this paper, these two analysis techniques of TOF-SIMS and XPS will be jointly applied to the analysis of the surface components of LED lead frame materials, especially the analysis of the trace element selenium (Se). We will apply TOF-SIMS for confirming the existence of the trace element Se and ensuring and improving the accuracy of XPS quantitative analysis results. XPS is often used to quantitatively analyze trace elements, but for some elements with complex peak positions, it is confusing and challenging to accurately determine the elements. However, through TOF-SIMS confirmation analysis, XPS's misjudgment of trace elements can be avoided, thereby obtaining more accurate quantitative analysis results. This paper successfully used TOF-SIMS and XPS testing methods to accurately and quantitatively analyze the surface components (Se, etc.) of the LED lead frame samples. TOF-SIMS has better sensitivity than XPS, but its quantitative analysis is not as good as XPS. The combination of the two techniques makes full use of their respective advantages, not only to avoid missing elements detected by XPS, but also to obtain more accurate XPS quantitative analysis results.

articleTitle: Enhanced Robustness of Interfacial Layer (IL) for PBTI Improvement of HfO2/TiN RMG Stacks by Low-Temperature Oxygen Plasma Treatment
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: In this paper, in order to enhance the quality of SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> chemical interfacial layer (IL) and get better PBTI characteristics of devices with HfO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/TiN stacks, the atom oxygen (O*) plasma treatment after IL growth is applied at low temperature (250°C) for 10 seconds. The experimental results show that equivalent oxide thickness (EOT) is increased about 0.12nm by O* plasma treatment, which is due to the SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> IL re-growth according to the TEM image and relationship between leakage (LKG) and EOT. The initial interface trap of device decreases about 60%, while the generated interface trap in PBTI at 125°C is obviously decreased, which is due to the increase of hydrogen in the interface between IL and silicon as shown in Secondary ion mass spectrometry (SIMS) data. The stress-induced leakage current (SILC) shows that the energy level of generated oxide trap in HfO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> by O* plasma treatment shifts to Ev of silicon about 0.04eV due to the nitrogen passivation in the oxide. This work gives a clue to improve the IL quality and PBTI using low-temperature thermal budget.

articleTitle: A Laboratory System for X-Ray Assisted Device Alteration (XADA)
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: Traditional backside optical fault-isolation (FI) techniques such as laser voltage probing (LVP), photon emission microscopy (PEM) and laser assisted device alteration (LADA) are no longer generally useful for 3-D stacked integrated circuits (IC) or backside power distribution (BPD) ICs due to near-infrared (NIR) blockage on both sides of the transistors. Recent work has demonstrated the effectiveness of using focused x-rays from a laboratory source for altering transistor threshold voltages (V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">T</inf>), changing ring oscillator (RO) frequencies, and inducing timing shifts in switching inverters. These results show that x-rays can be used for x-ray assisted device alteration (XADA) taking the place of LADA for 3D and BPD ICs in many debug and FI scenarios. Here, we present details of the first ever system developed and optimized for this emerging and ground-breaking application.

articleTitle: Analysis and Characterization Techniques for Wide Band Gap Semiconductor Materials
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: In this paper, based on the challenges of analysis and characterization of wide band gap semiconductor materials, the analysis techniques and characterization techniques were evaluated with SiC and GaN epitaxy wafers. Tool configuration and analysis results are discussed. A proposal of wafer characterization plan is given for the development of the fabrication technology of a wide band gap semiconductor device.

articleTitle: Embedded true random number generators enabled by hexagonal boron nitride memristors
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: Internet-of-things (IoT) devices require cheap, light, small and reliable true random number generators (TRNG) to encrypt data before transmission. Finding reliable randomness sources to seed the TRNG can be challenging in the presence of trade-offs such as power consumption, stability, and cost of the circuit implementation. We analyse the suitability of the random telegraph noise (RTN) signals of memristors made of two-dimensional (2D) layered hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN). After thorough evaluation of the noise characteristics, the h-BN memristor is connected to an analogue front-end and a microcontroller to fabricate a functional TRNG. Instead of using simulations as proof of potential functionality or bulky laboratory instrumentation, we provide an embedded TRNG which is scalable to the complementary-metal-oxide-semiconductor (CMOS) integration level and experimentally tested for randomness at the application level.

articleTitle: Analysis of Failure Mechanisms Occuring at Breakdown Voltage in power p-GaN HEMT
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: This study focuses on the drain-source breakdown voltage (V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">BR</inf>) of 100 V commercial p-GaN transistors. By presenting V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">BR</inf> values, showcasing device dispersion, and employing failure analysis (FA), we explore various physical degradation mechanisms. Investigating the degradation process from origin to defect manifestation enhances our understanding of GaN transistor limitations. Additionally, the paper highlights the adaptation of FA methodology based on defect nature, providing valuable insights for semiconductor device reliability improvement.

articleTitle: ESD Characteristics Improving of LVTSCR by Adding RC Triggering Circuit in 0.18 μm BCD Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: In this paper, Low Voltage Triggering SCR (LVTSCR) and RC-triggered LVTSCR are fabricated in a 0.18 μm Bipolar-CMOS-DMOS (BCD) process. TCAD simulation is introduced to study the ESD protection devices' working mechanism, while transmission line pulse (TLP) measuring system being used to characterize the devices' Electrostatic Discharge (ESD) characteristics. It is verified that the additional RC triggering circuit can reduce the devices' trigger voltage, and better ESD characteristics with higher holding voltage can be obtained through altering certain critical size.

articleTitle: Application of EBAC on Small Nets
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: EBAC is a very well understood technique. It is usually implemented on long traces where physical inspections are challenging. It is also implemented on short traces where a suspected resistive path is expected. In the current work, two very interesting cases where EBAC analysis implemented on much smaller length traces are presented.

articleTitle: Ge Depth Profile and Concentration Analysis by SIMS in Graded SiGe Epitaxial Film
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: Germanium dopant distribution and concentration in graded SiGe film have been analyzed by SIMS. Non-linearity in Ge and Si ion intensity response is noticed in the high Ge at% matrix under the Cs negative test condition, but not with + positive analysis. Since the profile shape is crucial for the graded SiGe epitaxial film, the paper discusses the gradual decreasing Ge depth profile measured under both Cs negative mode and positive mode. The accurate Ge at% quantification is achieved with XRD data as a reference.

articleTitle: Insights into Overcurrent-Induced Gate Breakdown and Failure Analysis of 1200 V SiC MOSFETs
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: Silicon carbide (SiC) metal-oxide-semiconductor field-effect transistors (MOSFETs) have been widely studied due to their high switching speed and high voltage resistance. However, its weak short current withstand capability makes SiC MOSFET face many failure problems. This paper presents the experimental results obtained from investigating the impact of overcurrent in SiC MOSFETs. The results indicate that a gate oxide burnout occurs by loading excessive current between source and drain. The failure mechanism is gate breakdown, which can be detected in-situ by monitoring the change in the electrical characteristic curves of SiC MOSFETs. To further analyze the irreversible damage caused by excessive current, thermally induced voltage alteration was initially utilized to locate the failure point. Then, a Focused Ion Beam (FIB) cut is performed, revealing severe burns at the gate area. According to the transmission electron microscopy (TEM) and TEM energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy results, it can be observed that the source metal diffuses into the trench of the SiC MOSFET, which is the origin physical failure point of the device.

articleTitle: PCB Surface Component Detection with Computer Vision Assisted Label Generation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: Surface component detection from optical images of Printed Circuit Boards (PCB) has been an effective approach to quickly identify and verify the electronic parts for ensuring PCB integrity in nowadays largely outsourced supply chain. Automated detection of PCB surface components based on emerging machine learning techniques is however hampered by the high variety among different component classes and the associated challenges in manual data labeling for training component detectors. In this paper, we first present a Computer Vision (CV) assisted approach to generate the label for PCB components, i.e., bounding boxes, from the design files, which is more efficient and reliable than data labeling based on human experience. With our collected PCB image dataset where labels are generated by our proposed CV-assisted approach, further evaluations have been performed to investigate the component detection performance using You-Only-Look-Once (YOLO) object detection models and to study the correlations between detection performance and class-specific dataset statistics.

articleTitle: Study of Efficient Design on Latchup in 130nm BCD Technology for High Voltage Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: We studied efficient design for high external latchup (ELUP) robustness in 130nm BCD technology under different Deep-Trench-Isolation (DTI) and N-EPI pickup configurations (NCOMP). We show DTI is very effective in reducing the space between I/O injector device and sensitive logic device, which is an ideal requirement for a lower footprint design with high latchup robustness. Furthermore, we demonstrate the critical role of DTI, when NCOMP around high voltage (HV) I/O FETs is biased at 0V, in latchup robustness of power management designs.

articleTitle: Degradation Study of GaN Cascode Devices Under High-Temperature Gate Bias Stress
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: This work investigates the degradation behaviors and mechanisms of GaN cascode devices under high-temperature off-state gate stress with different temperature, focusing on the analysis of threshold voltage (V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</inf>), on-resistance, and third quadrant output characteristics. High temperatures and electric fields stimulate the formation of more interface defects, leading to an increase in the negative shift of V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</inf>, which is caused by hole traps with an activation energy of 0.31 eV. This work provides insights for the reliability assessment and high-temperature application of GaN cascode devices.

articleTitle: Research on Failure Mechanism of SerDes Phase-Lock-Loop (PLL) Lose Lock
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: With the continuous improvement of chip performance, the requirement of Serializer-Deserializer (SerDes) performance is becoming higher and higher, faster transmission rate and lower power consumption, etc. The improvement of SerDes performance means more complicated structure accordingly and more challenges for failure analysis (FA). The paper analyzed the SerDes PLL lock loss case, which utilizing the FA method of dynamic emission microscope (dynamic EMMI), Conductive Atomic Force Microscope (C-AFM) and Nanoprobe to successfully found out the root cause of the failure and made an in-depth analysis of the failure mechanism. With the methods of circuit simulation analysis, circuit design issue is found and resulting in the risk of overvoltage in the use of the device, which eventually leads to the PLL lose lock.

articleTitle: Investigation of the Reliability of Different High-Resistance States in 1T1R Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: This research introduces a novel method, distinct from previous approaches, to achieve various high-resistance states. When operating in a high-resistance state (HRS) in a onetransistor - one - RRAM (1T1R) configuration, a significant voltage drop occurs across the transistor. This phenomenon makes it challenging to obtain diverse high-resistance states at different cut-off voltages. The proposed method addresses this issue, enabling the implementation of distinct high-resistance states. However, certain reliability issues still need clarification and further investigation, as discussed in the manuscript.

articleTitle: Overcoming Challenges in Foreign Material (FM) Analysis within BGA Packages using FTIR Spectroscopy with Solder Ball Shear
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR) is a valuable tool for identifying foreign materials (FMs) in semiconductor integrated circuits (ICs). Conventional FTIR techniques face limitations when analyzing FMs beneath Ball Grid Array (BGA) packages due to solder ball obstructions. Traditional methods are hindered by the physical barrier of solder balls. This paper presents an alternative approach utilizing solder ball shear followed by ATR FTIR analysis to effectively characterize FMs within BGA packages. Four common ball bond removal methods have been discussed and summarized demonstrating limitations to specifically FMs' obstacle conditions. Desoldering risks damaging the FM, while polishing and milling introduce contamination or flatness issues. The proposed ball shear method involves high-precision shearing the solder ball to expose the underlying FM, enabling direct contact with the ATR crystal for FTIR measurement. This approach avoids altering the FM's chemical structure while offering precise control over the shearing depth. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of this method in acquiring high-quality FTIR spectra of an embedded FM identified as Polyvinyl Formal (PVF). The characteristic peaks of the FM become clearly distinguishable after solder ball shear, significantly improving the signal-to-noise ratio and facilitating accurate identification.

articleTitle: Capacitive Coupling Voltage Contrast Contribution to PVC in Advanced SRAMs
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: Advances in SEM imaging voltage contrast of advanced technology node SRAMs are discussed. The use of large apertures, careful choice of plane of polish, and secondary electron detection modes in the SEM column may enable the triggering of Capacitive Coupling Voltage Contrast. An AI segmentation model that provides a quantitative quality factor for the images is presented.

articleTitle: XPS Characterization of Ag-Sn Backside Metallization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: X-ray Photoelectron Spectroscopy (XPS) was used to characterize Ag-Sn bilayer structure crucial for backside metallization (BSM) in power device. 1000 nm Sn layer followed by a 140 nm Ag layer was deposited using sputter deposition at 200°C. The XPS depth profile confirmed a 5 nm oxide layer at the surface and showcased Ag diffusion into Sn. Core-level binding energies and oxidation states of O 1s, C 1s, Sn 3d5/2, and Ag 3d species were analyzed through narrow scan XPS spectra, including depth profiling at the surface (cycle 0), 5 nm depth (cycle 1), and 40 nm depth (cycle 8). At cycle 0, a combination of pure Ag, pure Ag3Sn, pure Sn, and other species was observed, with atomic concentrations of 1.29%, 4.21%, 5.56%, and 88.94%, respectively. The atomic concentrations of pure Ag, pure Ag3Sn, and pure Sn were 28.69%, 19.64%, and 51.68% respectively at cycle 1, and 38.02%, 13.16%, and 48.82% respectively at cycle 8. The lower concentration of AgO (17.86%) compared to SnO (31.84%) at cycle 0 and the consistent lower concentration of Ag than Sn at cycles 0, 1, and 8 suggested that complete Ag diffusion into Sn, concurrent with Ag3Sn intermetallic compound formation. The study highlights the role of XPS in understanding Ag-Sn bilayer thin films and illustrate the contribution of interdiffusion mechanism to Ag3Sn intermetallic compound formation.

articleTitle: GaN Epitaxial Layer Dislocation Characterization Using ECCI and TEM
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: Gallium nitride (GaN) is a representative material of the third-generation semiconductor. The growth of GaN heteroepitaxial layers on substrates often leads to dislocations due to lattice mismatch. This paper presents a comprehensive characterization method of these defects using two kinds of electron microscopes, which are commonly available in analytical laboratories. Specifically, we used the electron channeling contrast imaging (ECCI) method based on a dual beam electron microscope system to observe dislocations from the sample surface. We discussed key parameters for acquiring optimal ECCI images and subsequently prepared planar and cross-section lamella samples for analysis at the nano-scale level using transmission electron microscopy (TEM). Our study provides valuable insights into GaN dislocation characterization utilizing two types of electron microscopes, while also discussing image conditions that can serve as a useful reference for semiconductor researchers and engineers conducting similar investigations.

articleTitle: Development of FIB Sampling Technology for large area TEM Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: In the semiconductor industry which conducts ultra-fine processes, Transmission Electron Microscope (TEM) which can analyze down to ‘nm’ units or less, has become very important. Focused Ion Beam (FIB) allows engineers to produce specimens so that they can perform TEM analysis on specific areas they want. However, considering that the TEM analysis area size through the traditional FIB method is 4um, the traditional method not only provides insufficient data to determine the direction of the process, but also has the problem of creating multiple samples to see the large area. This paper will discuss how to produce a ‘large area TEM specimen’ which is more than 5 times wider than that of existing TEM specimen through bending control. The bending phenomenon has been a problem for large area specimens and we could overcome it by introducing the concept of ‘support’ into FIB sampling technology. Through this study, the limitations of analysis coverage, which had been pointed out as the limitations of TEM analysis, were overcome, and the foundation for TEM Massive Critical Dimension (CD) measurement has been laid.

articleTitle: Enhancing the Thermal Conductivity of Graphene-based Thermal Interface Materials by Polyimide Fiber Intercalation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: Temperature is an important factor affecting the reliability of electronic components. High temperature environments have a direct negative impact on the performance and lifetime of electronic devices. Graphene, a remarkable two-dimensional carbon material renowned for its exceptional in-plane thermal conductivity properties, faces a significant challenge due to the high phonon transport barrier at the van der Waals interface between its layers. This poses a limitation for meeting the heat dissipation requirements of cutting-edge electronic devices. In this study, a graphene composite film with polyimide (PI) fiber intercalation is presented. Graphene oxide (GO) and PI composite films were obtained by solution blending of PI fibers and GO. Subsequently, the GO/PI film was graphitised and calendered at high temperature to obtain the dense g-GO/PI film. The PI fiber intercalation constructs a three-dimensional thermal conductivity network that enables the g-GO/PI film to have high in-plane thermal conductivity (1406 W m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">‐1</sup>K-<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>) and through-plane thermal conductivity (21.3 W m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">‐1</sup> K-<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>). The exceptional thermal conductivity of the graphitized GO/PI film (g-GO/PI) as a thermal interface material confirms its superior thermal management capability compared to copper foil. This presents an enticing prospect for the integration of advanced thermal management systems in future high-performance flexible electronic devices.

articleTitle: Characterization of Stress Voltage/Time-Dependent Dynamic RDS,ON in 600 V-Rated GaN Power Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: The effects of off-state stress voltage (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V_{DS,OFF}$</tex>) and time (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$t_{stress}$</tex>) on dynamic on-resistance (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R_{DS,ON}$</tex>) are investigated in 600 V-rated GaN power devices. A modified double-pulse test (DPT) circuit and the multigroups DPT method are used to evaluate the dynamic <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R_{DS,ON}$</tex> degradation under hard-switching conditions. The findings highlight <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$t_{stress}$</tex> as a crucial factor leading to either monotonic increases or non-monotonic variations in Schottky-type p-GaN gate HEMT dynamic <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R_{DS,ON}$</tex> with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V_{DS,OFF}$</tex>. Moreover it is found that the p-drain structure of hybrid drain-gate injection transistor effectively mitigates dynamic <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R_{DS,ON}$</tex> degradation at higher <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V_{DS,OFF}$</tex>. Consequently, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$t_{stress}$</tex> should be carefully considered, guided by the mechanisms identified in relation to dynamic <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R_{DS,ON}$</tex> degradation.

articleTitle: The Effects of Localized Rework on Microstructural Evolution of Interfacial IMC in Mirrored BGA Electronic Packaging
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: The hot air rework soldering process is a wellestablished practice in PCB assembly for rectifying faulty electronic components and minimizing defects. However, there remains a limited understanding of the microstructural evolution occurring in reworked, adjacent, and mirror-side components of a mirrored BGA electronic packaging. This paper aims to address this gap by analyzing the microstructural evolution of interfacial intermetallic compounds (IMCs) in these components during the hot air rework soldering, employing scanning electron microscopy (SEM). The findings reveal that the localized rework process caused grain coarsening in the reworked component and its adjacent and mirrored components. This phenomenon is attributed to an increase in Cu concentration in the solder melt, promoting larger Cu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf>Sn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf> IMC grain growth. Interestingly, the assessment of Cu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf>Sn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf> grain size in the mirrored components of the PCB reveals larger grains compared to the reworked side. This discrepancy can be attributed to the slower cooling rate experienced by the mirrored components during localized reflow, leading to grain boundary diffusion of Cu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf>Sn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf> grains, as evidenced by observed necking and grain coalescence.

articleTitle: Warpage Improvement for Die Thinning using Thermal Flattening Technique for high Die-to-Package Area Ratio on FCBGA Package
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: Si die warpage or curvature on a flip-chip technology is commonly occurred once the Si chip is attached on a package interposer substrate in the presence of high temperature during the reflow process. In this paper, the challenges introduced by high die-to-package area ratio on the severity of warpage on Flip-Chip Ball Grid Array (FCBGA) packages are highlighted. The effects of severe warpage in mechanical Computer Numerical Control (CNC) die thinning process on die thickness uniformity and grinding time are examined. With high warpage, it is difficult to achieve good thinning uniformity where the silicon final thickness is the same throughout the die area. Additional thinning is needed for more precise grinding which will take more time. To reduce the warpage of FCBGA packages, this work proposed a thermal flattening technique that applied vertical downward force using a tensile tester. The method and outcomes of the flattening process are discussed and its main goals to improve post-thinning die uniformity and warpage are demonstrated within certain identified constraints.

articleTitle: Degradation Analysis of Schottky GaN HEMT between Hard Switching and Soft Switching Stress
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: In this study, the degradation trend between hard switching and soft switching under the long-term reliability test of schottky GaN HEMT is analyzed. The degradation in the output current becomes more severe as the switching waveform transitions from soft switching to that of hard switching. However, there is an unusual trend in the positive threshold voltage, characterized by an initial rise followed by a decline. The deterioration of soft switching is dominated by the off-state leakage, where the gate leakage and the source leakage cause the electron injection into the AlGaN and GaN layers. In the case of the hard switching, the degradation is maintained by hot electrons inject into the GaN layer, and the generated holes by the trap-assisted thermionic emission (TA-TFE) recombine with the electrons injected into the GaN layer under the gate. Long-term DC stress is also employed to clarify this unusual trend. This degradation results from the chain reaction of the rapid switching between off-state and on-state, making it challenging to be observed under DC stress.

articleTitle: Degradation Comparison of P-type Thin Film Transistor under Dynamic Gate Pulsed Stress
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: The degradation of p-type poly-Si TFTs under various dynamic gate pulse stresses was investigated. We clarify the impacts of pulse rising time <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\boldsymbol {t}_{r})$</tex> and pulse falling time <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\boldsymbol t_{f)}$</tex> on device degradation, respectively. Under dynamic PBTI stress or dynamic gate voltage stresses swinging between the on-state and off-state, both the electrons trapping into gate oxide and the traps generation near the source/drain are responsible for the two-stage degradation, which can be explained by the hot carrier (HC) effect using the nonequilibrium pn junction degradation model. To suppress the dynamic degradation, a new four-terminal TFT is designed with a carrier injection structure. A relieved degradation with an additional hump phenomenon can be observed for the first time under the same pulsed gate stress since the channel state can follow the pulse transition, eliminating the HC effect. More electrons trapping at the channel side is proposed to explain the hump phenomenon and is proven by the TCAD simulation.

articleTitle: Optical Power Degradation Related to Turn-On in Commercial 265 nm UV-C LEDs
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: In this work, we investigated the optical power drops present after the turn-on of high-power commercial UV-C LEDs. We demonstrated that degradation occurs in correspondence with the turn-on of the device. By slowing the turn-on transient, 5.8 mA/s rate, we demonstrated that even a gradual increase in the current could not prevent the phenomenon, indicating that it is not correlated to the sudden change in temperature and electric field. From thermal characterization and voltage transients, we extrapolated a high thermal coefficient for this UV LED with respect to the visible counterpart. Moreover, from a visual inspection, we observed a degradation of the encapsulation, which could be caused by both the high temperatures reached and by the energy of the emitted photons.

articleTitle: Effects of the Interfacial Layer on the Leakage Current and Hysteresis Behaviour of Ferroelectric Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: Data collected from electrical characterization on Metal - Ferroelectric - Insulator - Semiconductor (MFIS) and Metal- Ferroelectric - Metal (MIM) Ferroelectric (FE) devices are compared. Although numerous studies exist on both device structures, a direct comparison of the differences in the signatures of degradation during electrical characterization is lacking. In this work, analysis of Interrupted CVS and transient current measurements using the PUND waveform alongside pulsed cycling stress indicate that the interfacial layer (IL) in the MFIS structure is the origin of the discrepancies and that the IL influences the collected data through increasing charge trapping and defect generation, as well as modifying the band energy diagram of the device stack. The qualitative studies of electrical characterization data provide a starting point for quantitative analysis and identification of the physical mechanisms underlying the observed degradation.

articleTitle: Analysis of Etcher Configuration on Part Marking Characteristics for Counterfeit Identification
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: Laser mark analysis is common when analyzing suspect counterfeit electronics, but prior mark analysis has been limited to subjective quality evaluation or visual comparison against golden samples. In an effort to identify objective metrics for part mark analysis, we explore how laser etcher characteristics and configurations impact a mark's appearance. We first analyze the theoretical impact of etcher configuration changes on mark characteristics, then conduct a controlled study of fifty integrated circuits etched with different settings to assess which settings can be discerned in low-magnification images. Our study suggests that observable part marking characteristics can indicate part provenance and inform objective, data-driven decisions about integrated circuit authenticity.

articleTitle: Reliability of Reconfigurable Field Effect Transistors: Early Analysis of Bias Temperature Instability
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: Bias temperature instability is a common relia-bility issue in Metal Oxide Semiconductor Field Effect Transistors used in silicon integrated circuits. When transferred to in-dustrial processing platforms, also emerging electron devices need to be characterized under gate bias stress, in order to reveal their behavior in realistic application scenarios. In this work, we present an early evaluation of bias temperature insta-bility on three-gated Reconfigurable Field Effect Transistors. These emerging nanoelectronics devices allow to set and dynam-ically change their polarity into either n-type or p-type conduction modes, enabling also a multi-V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">T</inf> behavior. The polarity con-trol feature, opposite to conventional MOSFETs where the device nature is set to either n-type or p-type by the fabrication, implies that both conduction modes of a Reconfigurable Field Effect Transistor can be influenced by stress profiles of a given polarity. Our experiments showed that NBTI has a stronger effect on both conduction modes of such a transistor, independent of the V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">T</inf> mode in which the device is operated, as compared to PBTI. Moreover, n-type programmed devices showed a greater degradation of their threshold voltages. Finally, we observed that the high-V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">T</inf> mode is more prone to be subjected to sub-threshold slope degradation compared to the low-V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">T</inf> mode.

articleTitle: Improving 3D NAND Flash Memories Reliability: a Cross-Layer Perspective
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: The 3D NAND Flash memory technology is the main building block of storage architectures such as multimedia cards and Solid-State Drives. Applications ranging from mobile to high-performance computing are continuously calling for an increased storage density, requiring massive scaling efforts at the device and array level. This leads to a natural degradation of the functional metrics of the technology while exposing new reliability issues that jeopardize the inherent memory trade-off with performance. A simple device optimization would be insufficient to tackle the problem. In this work, we show through some case studies how a cross-layer approach spanning from devices and circuits to system-level optimizations is mandatory for future storage systems development.

articleTitle: Improved Yield Prediction and Failure Analysis in Semiconductor Manufacturing with XGBoost and Shapley Additive exPlanations Models
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: In the domain of semiconductor manufacturing, the accurate prediction of wafer yield and subsequent failure analysis (FA) are of critical importance with respect to the assurance of product quality and the optimization of production processes. However, traditional methods frequently exhibit a high dependency on engineering expertise, modest accuracy, and an inability to adapt swiftly to manufacturing environment changes. To address these issues, this study introduces an advanced machine learning (ML) model that combines Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) with XGBoost. This innovative approach is adept at capturing the complex non-linear relationships between wafer acceptance test (WAT) data and wafer yield. The integration of PSO enables effective WAT feature selection while fine-tuning the hyperparameters of the XGBoost, thereby resulting in a significant improvement in model performance. The proposed PSO-XGBoost model exhibits remarkable accuracy (96.4%), AUC-score (91.4%), F1-measure (97.9%), precision (97.2%), and recall (98.6%). Moreover, the integration of the Shapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) method facilitates the interpretability of the model, elucidating the critical WAT parameters that influence yield on both global and local scales. This study not only provides a cost-effective methodology that reduces reliance on human expertise but also paves the way for the expanded role of artificial intelligence (AI) in enhancing semiconductor manufacturing processes. This represents a new era in the field of smart manufacturing and quality assurance.

articleTitle: Advances in High-Resolution Non-Destructive Defect Detection and Localization Enhanced by Intelligent Signal Processing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: In development and production of microelectronics products the assessment of the condition of either the full component or only specific parts is of high relevance. To allow for screening and monitoring and to leave the part unaltered the inspection techniques are required to operate non-destructively. While this allows for full-cover final inspection it also enables repetitive monitoring beneficial for the exploration of material interactions, potential subsequent defect formations and consequently for failure isolation. With increasing complexity inherent in advancing microelectronic technologies, high reliability, robustness and thus, successful failure analysis is essential. The correspondingly shrinking feature sizes and the involvement of heterogeneous materials highly challenge existing techniques. Furthermore, the interpretation of the acquired data becomes increasingly difficult requiring specifically skilled operating personal. In previous studies machine learning (ML) approaches have been developed and evaluated for their ability to analyze signals acquired by scanning acoustic microscopy (SAM) with the goal of automated defect detection, characterization, and failure isolation. The present paper investigates different ML architectures to analyze the time signals after transformation into the spectral- and wavelet domains. Results showed that 2D CNNs analyzing the acquired acoustic signals in the wavelet domain representation performed best, however at the expense of additional computational effort. Furthermore, ML-based analysis was explored for its potential to locate and isolate electrically active defects in the depth-dimension based on thermal emissions using lock-in thermography (LIT). Obtained LIT-related results are promising, however require further research to fully enfold its potential. It was further found that transfer properties of the inspection tools interfere with the defect specific signal features and thus so far tie the trained models to the specific equipment used. Future work should therefore focus on removing the specific tool related transfer characteristics of the equipment from the measurement data to allow for intra-tool compatibility and thus a more generalized application. (Abstract)

articleTitle: Analysis of Distinct Degradation Behavior in LTPS TFTs Under Hot Carrier Condition with Varying Gate Voltage
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: In this research, a distinct degradation behavior is observed in the low-temperature polycrystalline-silicon thin-film transistor under hot carrier condition with varying driving gate voltages. The factor causing this distinct degradation behavior can be generalized into two terms. The first term is the gate-to-drain voltage, which dominates the degree of impact ionization, controlling the generation of electron-hole pairs. Furthermore, the gate-to-drain voltage also influences the distribution of electric field direction and strength at the drain edge, governing the trapping of electrons into the gate insulator at the drain edge and at the buffer. The second factor contributing to the distinct degradation behavior is the stress current induced thermal in the channel. The current flowing in the channel induces Joule heating, leading to the occurrence of negative bias temperature instability in the channel. Consequently, higher driving currents exacerbate the degradation associated with negative bias temperature instability. In summary, the degradation behavior in the low-temperature polycrystalline-silicon thin-film transistor under hot carrier conditions with varying driving gate voltages is influenced simultaneously by the gate-to-drain voltage and the driving current.

articleTitle: Parasitic Circus: On the Feasibility of Golden-Free PCB Verification
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: Printed circuit boards (PCBs) are an integral part of electronic systems. Hence, verifying their physical integrity in the presence of supply chain attacks (e.g., tampering and counterfeiting) is of utmost importance. Recently, tamper detection techniques grounded in impedance characterization of PCB's Power Delivery Network (PDN) have gained prominence due to their global detection coverage, non-invasive, and low-cost nature. Similar to other physical verification methods, these techniques rely on the existence of a physical golden sample for signature comparisons. However, having access to a physical golden sample for golden signature extraction is not feasible in many real-world scenarios. In this work, we assess the feasibility of eliminating a physical golden sample and replacing it with a simulated golden signature obtained by the PCB design files. By performing extensive simulation and measurements on an in-house designed PCB, we demonstrate how the parasitic impedance of the PCB components plays a major role in reaching a successful verification. Based on the obtained results and using statistical metrics, we show that we can mitigate the discrepancy between collected signatures from simulation and measurements.

articleTitle: Denoising of Transmission Electron Microscopy Images for Atomic Defect Identification
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: Two-dimensional (2D) materials possess remarkable electrical, mechanical, thermal, and optical properties, making them applicable in the fields of electronics and optoelectronics. Atomic defects could significantly affect device performance and reliability. Clearly identify and analysis of atomic defects in 2D materials is crucial. Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) with atomic resolution serves as an ideal method for the defect characterization of 2D materials. However, TEM images often suffer from various types of noise, which severely hampers the analysis of 2D materials. In this study, we propose a neural network based on the optimized CycleGAN architecture for TEM image denoising even when obtaining strictly paired datasets for TEM is challenging. The optimized CycleGAN model with attention gate could improve the signal-to-noise ratio and structural similarity of the denoised images. The effectiveness of this method was validated on the scanning transmission electron microscopy image dataset. Enhancing the visibility of atomic contrast and improving the accuracy of identifying individual atomic structures are achieved by removing the surrounding noise from the original image.

articleTitle: Reliability Analysis and Comparison on Electromigration of SACQ and SAC305 Solder Balls
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: In this paper, the electromigration (EM) analysis of Sn-4.0Ag-0.5Cu-3.0Bi-0.05Ni (SACQ) and Sn-3.0Ag-0.5Cu-0.05Ni (SAC305) solder balls is investigated. To study the EM reliability performance, multi-level accelerated life tests are designed. A novel temperature calibration method is proposed to characterize the Joule heating effect of solder balls when subjected to high currents. An EM prediction model, based on the modified Black equation, is employed to compare the reliability properties of SACQ and SAC305. As per the results of reliability statistics, the activation energy of SACQ and SAC305 is estimated to be 0.97 ± 0.2 eV and 0.78 ± 0.1 eV, respectively, with the current coefficient being 11.9 ± 1 for SACQ and 3.15 ± 0.6 for SAC305. The failure mechanism is discussed using optical microscope, scanning electron microscope, and energy dispersive X-rays. The observed failure results of the SAC-based solder system concur with the Liquid-solid failure mode, as portrayed in the extant literature. Moreover, this work delves into the prevailing polarity effect inherent in Cu/Sn interconnects and the EM reliability augmentation fostered by Bi-doping.

articleTitle: New Perspective on Understanding Contact between Metal and Oxide Through Atomistic Modeling: A Case Study on Tin Oxide in Contact with Common Metals
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: Remarkable efforts have been devoted to the detection, location, and resolution of electrical contact failures. However, because of the complex interplay of physical, mechanical, and electrical factors as well as the continuous miniaturization of electronic devices to the nanoscale, current methods that rely on conventional contact resistance measurements face significant limitations. By adopting the approach of atomistic modeling, our study tackles this persistent issue by providing a new perspective on fundamentals of contact mechanisms. As an example, the contact between common metals and tin oxide is systematically evaluated and compared by examining the charge transfer and bonding at the interface. The obtained theoretical results serve as the principles for explaining the contact behavior of such materials systems and provide more insights and practical guidance on materials selection, troubleshooting and problem solving, as well as device design.

articleTitle: Towards an FA ChatBot with Retrieval-Augmented Language Modeling
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: Failure Analysis (FA) data storages, like databases or file shares, host a lot of textual data comprising important information about products, best practices, or past cases. FA engineers require this information at their fingertips to accomplish their tasks efficiently. However, common keyword search interfaces provided by most information systems and databases are insufficient as they force an engineer to formulate a correct query, read returned documents, and manually extract required knowledge from them. In this paper, we suggest a cost-effective approach that augments retrieval systems with the capabilities of modern Large Language Models (LLMs) to provide straight-to-point answers to engineers’ questions. Preliminary evaluation shows that the suggested system can generate high-quality responses to a set of simple benchmark queries but also lacks complex reasoning capabilities for answering complex queries.

articleTitle: Enhanced Yield Prediction in Semiconductor Manufacturing: Innovative Strategies for Imbalanced Sample Management and Root Cause Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on the Physical and Failure Analysis of Integrated Circuits (IPFA)
abstract: This paper presents a novel framework for predicting semiconductor wafer yields using Wafer Acceptance Test (WAT) parameters, addressing the challenge of unbalanced datasets commonly encountered in wafer manufacturing. WAT, essential for monitoring process stability and cost control, and Chip Probing (CP) testing, which assesses the functionality of each Die on a wafer, are integral to ensuring product quality. However, the yield data, indicating the proportion of functional chips post-CP testing, often suffer from data imbalance, skewing machine learning predictions towards the majority class and reducing model accuracy. To overcome this, the study leverages Generative Adversarial Networks (GAN) to generate balanced samples by creating minority class samples for model training. This approach not only mitigates the costs associated with CP testing but also facilitates early fault detection in wafer manufacturing. Through extensive experimentation with real in-dustrial WAT and yield data, the proposed method demonstrates a significant improvement in model performance, enhancing it by approximately 7% and achieving an Area Under the Curve (AUC) of over 0.95. Additionally, the SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) model is employed within the framework to rapidly analyze and identify faults impacting yield, further contributing to the efficiency of semiconductor production processes.
